conviction_note: Baseline median reaction is 6.08% with 4 of 8 prints up (cadence flagged implausible so I treat the base rate loosely); I take a moderate positive because the company raised roughly $100m in a 5.6m-share marketed secondary at $18.00 on 2026-06-30, signed a material definitive agreement two days later that nothing in the capture describes, and now trades at $15.96 - 11% below the deal price with the acquisition still unannounced nine weeks on, making this print the venue where the cash gets accounted for.

findings.finding: Mama's Creations priced a 5.6m-share spot secondary at $18.00 on 2026-06-30 (range $17.50-18.50, William Blair and DA Davidson joint books), the stock fell 12.3% on the announcement, and it now enters the print at $15.96 - 11.3% below the price every institution in that deal paid nine weeks ago - with roughly $100m of undeployed cash and the acquisition the raise was understood to fund still unannounced.

findings.why_not_priced: The offering is wire copy; the position of the deal buyers is not, and nothing in the capture computes it. A freshly placed institutional book sitting 11% underwater into the first print since the raise is the marginal holder, and the reason the price fell 12.8% over twenty sessions with, in the corpus's own words on 2026-08-27, 'can't find a reason for the drop'. There is no news-search coverage of this ticker at all (n_queries=0 in every sweep), so no preview links the raise, the undeployed cash and the print.
findings.independence: A separate corpus item on 2026-07-21 makes the same observation independently - 'stock trading at 17$, meaning it dropped below the 18$ price of the recent share issuance. This will head back above as soon as the company releases info on the new acquisition' - docs/170806f7b3373558655fba2c2c0b8739efd7da18.txt

findings.finding: An 8-K with items 1.01, 8.01 and 9.01 - a material definitive agreement plus other events - was filed on 2026-07-01, the day after the offering closed, and its contents appear nowhere in the 57-item capture; nine weeks later the retail base is still 'waiting for the big news on the company's next acquisitions'.
findings.corpus_ref: filings.json, 8-K dated 2026-07-01 with items '1.01,8.01,9.01'; docs/170806f7b3373558655fba2c2c0b8739efd7da18.txt entry dated 2026-07-08T20:02:36Z
findings.why_not_priced: The body is not stored and no observed source describes it, so the market's read of what was signed the day after a $100m raise is invisible in this corpus. An item 1.01 filed into that sequence is most naturally a purchase agreement or a credit facility, either of which would be reported on and quantified at this print. The direction is uncertain, which is why the range is wide, but the existence of an undescribed material agreement immediately after the raise is a fact the previews cannot have weighed because there are no previews.
findings.independence: none - shares the EDGAR index and the same Stocktwits body as finding 1; collapse to one cluster.

searched_and_found_nothing: the body of the 2026-07-01 item-1.01 8-K, the biggest gap in this hunt
any 8-K after 2026-07-07 (item 5.07, annual meeting results) - so no acquisition announcement, no guidance update and no pre-release in the eight weeks into the print
any 13D or activist position; only passive 13G/13G/A filings on 2026-07-16 and 2026-07-31
any explanation for the -12.8% twenty-day slide beyond the deal overhang
any news-wire coverage, consensus estimate or sell-side preview: n_queries=0 in every sweep, so no view of what the raise is expected to earn
any figure for shares outstanding, so I could not size the $100m raise against the equity precisely
baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-up (-12.8% over twenty sessions) and against the last print (-11.12%), and it argues the slide is deal-overhang mechanics rather than deteriorating trade.
corpus_limits: No option chain, so no implied move or skew. No news search was run for this ticker; the entire non-filing corpus is one Stocktwits thread heavily polluted with unrelated chatter and one confusion with 'Mamata Machinery', which I discarded. No 8-K or 424B5 body is stored. The baseline's cadence verdict is 'unknown' (56-day inferred cadence), so the reaction history is a loose guide only. This is an amc print, so the 2026-09-03 sweep and price bar are pre-event and admissible; no item in this capture carried a non-empty tripwire_tells.
